import { CodeBlock } from '../../components/ui';

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="two-independent-axes"><a href="#two-independent-axes">Two independent axes</a></h2>

Implementation status and evidence provenance answer different questions. Current, partial, and proposed describe a capability’s lifecycle. Measured, reported, and target describe the provenance of a numerical figure in the existing MLAI contracts.

A reported capability is not necessarily a measured performance result. A target is not an achieved outcome. A synthetic example may be useful for explaining an interface, but it must not be presented as measurement.

</section>

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="what-counts-as-evidence"><a href="#what-counts-as-evidence">What counts as evidence</a></h2>

A README can establish what a project documents. A test file can establish the conditions it is intended to exercise. A successful test run must identify its revision and environment. A meaningful benchmark needs more than an isolated number.

- Identify the exact source revision and execution date.
- Record hardware, toolchain, inputs, and relevant configuration.
- Describe the method, uncertainty, and limitations.
- Keep an artifact that another reader can inspect.

</section>

<section className="doc-section">

<h2 id="what-this-site-does-not-prove"><a href="#what-this-site-does-not-prove">What this site does not prove</a></h2>

This website publishes no independently measured ABI, WDBX, or Gama performance results. It does not verify production deployments, regulatory certifications, general native GPU execution, or model intelligence.

A functional documentation search and an attractive architecture diagram are website features. They are not proof of the underlying projects’ runtime capabilities. The trust page intentionally labels source-documented behavior and the limitations that accompany it.

</section>
